message.content:
To pull the CNAME records for **sample.com** from VirusTotal you’ll hit the *DNS records* endpoint for that domain.  
Here’s what you need to do:

```bash
# Replace YOUR_API_KEY with your real key – never share it publicly!
curl -s \
     -H "x-apikey: YOUR_API_KEY" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records"
```

The JSON response looks roughly like this:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "record_id_1",
      "type": "dns_record",
      "attributes": {
        "name": "www.sample.com",
        "type": "CNAME",
        "value": "alias.example.net",
        ...
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "record_id_2",
      "type": "dns_record",
      "attributes": {
        "name": "mail.sample.com",
        "type": "MX",
        ...
      }
    },
    …
  ]
}
```

**Extract only the IDs of the CNAME records**

1. Parse the `data` array.  
2. For each item, check `attributes.type`.  
3. If it equals `"CNAME"`, take the value of `id`.

In shell scripting you could do something like:

```bash
ids=$(curl -s -H "x-apikey: YOUR_API_KEY" \
          "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records" |
       jq -r '.data[] | select(.attributes.type=="CNAME") | .id')

echo "$ids"
```

That will print one line per CNAME record ID, e.g.:

```
record_id_1
record_id_7
…
```

Those IDs are the “related object IDs” you asked for. Remember to keep your API key confidential.
